subject: BrightLeaf MAP: performance benchmarking plan + long-context test schedule
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@brightleaf.ai>
To: jordan_blake@redwoodai.com
Cc: alicia.gomez@brightleaf.ai, procurement@brightleaf.ai
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP proposal - performance & long-context tests

Hi Jordan,

Thanks again for the demo last week — BrightLeaf is excited about Redwood's serving story. We'd like to lock a Mutual Action Plan (MAP) that includes a performance benchmark (latency/throughput/TTFT) and long-context validation. Key constraints on our side:

- We expect prompt sizes to vary: 70% of traffic <= 2k tokens, 20% ~ 8k tokens, 10% up to 48k in peak analytic queries.
- We need TTFT and sustained throughput numbers at concurrency levels from 1 to 32.
- KV cache behavior is critical: many queries are prefix-shared across sessions.
- Procurement wants an initial close timeline for contract approval by 2027-03-28.

Can you propose a test matrix, milestones (who does what), and a preliminary run schedule this week? We'll attach our example prompt set next.

Best,
Samir
Samir Patel
Head of Product, BrightLeaf Analytics
From: jordan_blake@redwoodai.com
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@brightleaf.ai>
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwoodai.com, karthik_iyer@redwoodai.com, david_kim@redwoodai.com
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 10:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP proposal - performance & long-context tests

Samir — thanks, this is clear and actionable. Draft MAP below (high level) and a proposed benchmark/eval plan. Attaching a MAP spreadsheet for sign-off.

MAP milestones (owner / target date):
1) Sign MAP (BrightLeaf / Redwood) — target 2027-03-18 — owner: procurement / jordan_blake
2) Test matrix & dataset handoff — target 2027-03-16 — owner: BrightLeaf (prompt set)
3) Dry run (1st pass) — target 2027-03-17 — owner: Redwood SRE/bench team
4) Full benchmark (3 runs per config) — target 2027-03-18 to 2027-03-19 — owner: Redwood infra
5) Results review & optimization suggestions — target 2027-03-22 — owner: Redwood (neha & karthik)

Benchmark scope / test matrix (summary):
- Models: rdx-13b-quant, rdx-33b, rdx-70b (verified variants).
- Max sequence lengths tested: 2k (baseline), 8k, 32k, 48k, 64k (stress).
- Prompt distribution: 70% <=2k, 20% 2k-8k, 9% 8k-32k, 1% >32k. (BrightLeaf provided example set.)
- Concurrency sweep: 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32. Run each with 3 independent runs.
- Metrics captured: TTFT (time-to-first-token), token P50/P95 latency, end-to-end time, tokens/sec (throughput), memory footprint, and KV cache hit/miss latencies.
- KV cache experiments: cold vs warm sessions, repeated-prefix ratio 0%, 50%, 90%.

Deliverables:
- CSV of raw latency traces + aggregated percentiles.
- Per-route cost estimate (tokens/sec / GPU-hour).
- Optimization suggestions (batching, quantization, routing).

Quick notes on execution: we'll run on dedicated infer pool (A100-80GB equiv). For long sequences we may throttle batch size to avoid OOM — we'll record per-run batch sizes.

Next steps: please sign the attached MAP sheet and confirm availability for dataset handoff today. If procurement needs a faster close, let's escalate and include a one-time evaluation credit.

Thanks — sending this to the team to start scheduling the dry run.

— Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: neha_kapoor@redwoodai.com
To: jordan_blake@redwoodai.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwoodai.com, david_kim@redwoodai.com
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP proposal - performance & long-context tests

Jordan / team — a few technical clarifications before we schedule runs:

1) TTFT measurement: we should capture both (a) server-side decode start and (b) client-observed first byte; I'll log both and mark which is used for SLA claims.
2) For >32k tests we need to define padding policy and tokenizer overhead; BrightLeaf should indicate whether their prompts include long structured contexts (JSON blobs) or many short concatenated messages.
3) Concurrency test harness: I'll use k6 + our continuous batching shim to simulate mixed prompt distribution. For 32/64k sequences we'll drop batch size to 1 or 2 to avoid KV evictions.
4) KV cache instrumentation: add a histogram of KV lookups per request and a per-request cache-hit boolean so we can show delta in TTFT and token latency.

I'll prepare the exact run commands and a reproducibility checklist. Also adding a quick smoke run (10 requests / config) to validate memory behavior before full runs.

-Neha
Neha Kapoor
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

From: jordan_blake@redwoodai.com
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@brightleaf.ai>, Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@brightleaf.ai>, procurement@brightleaf.ai
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwoodai.com, karthik_iyer@redwoodai.com, david_kim@redwoodai.com
Date: Thu, 18 Mar 2027 14:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP proposal - performance & long-context tests — dry run results + agreed MAP

Team — quick update after the dry run and initial benchmark pass. Attached: brightleaf_benchmark_results_summary.pdf and test_matrix_long_context.csv (raw traces attached as CSVs in Drive). Summary below.

Dry run summary (representative numbers, A100-80GB equivalent):
- Model: rdx-33b, batch-size tuned per-seq-length.
- TTFT (server decode start / client-first-byte):
  - 2k seqs: P50 110ms / P95 210ms ; client-first-byte ~ P50 140ms
  - 8k seqs: P50 180ms / P95 380ms ; client-first-byte ~ P50 210ms
  - 32k seqs: P50 320ms / P95 720ms ; client-first-byte ~ P50 360ms
  - 48k seqs: P50 480ms / P95 1.2s ; signs of memory pressure at sustained concurrency >8
- Throughput (tokens/sec raw, single GPU):
  - 2k mix (70%): sustained 210 tokens/s at concurrency 8 (batching active)
  - 8k-heavy: sustained 95 tokens/s at concurrency 4
  - 32k-long: ~42 tokens/s when batching disabled (batch size 1-2)
- Concurrency: stable up to 16 for mixed workloads; sustained 32 causes queueing and elevated P95 (>2s) for long sequences.
- KV cache impact: warm-prefix runs reduced TTFT by ~1.8x for repeated prefixes (50% prefix-repeat workload). Cache hit reduces per-token latency variance.
- Max seq behavior: beyond 48k we observed OOM on rdx-70b at default batch sizes; we recommend a configured max-seq of 64k with enforced batch size <=1 and progressive fallback to a longer-window-optimized variant.

Action items agreed:
- BrightLeaf to sign MAP sheet (brightleaf_map_v1.xlsx) by EOD 2027-03-18 (procurement).
- Redwood to run full benchmark (3 runs per config) 2027-03-18 -> 2027-03-19; deliverables by 2027-03-22.
- Redwood will provide a one-page cost estimate for the full benchmark by 2027-03-17 (attached in drive).

Notes for final report: include per-run raw traces, aggregator scripts, and a short section on best-practice config for large-token workloads (KV tuning, batch size caps, and tokenization tips).

If procurement confirms the MAP signature, we'll proceed to the full runs tonight. Thanks all — feel free to call if you want to review the PDF now.

— Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
